Ujfeherto Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Újfehértó, Hungary

Demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Újfehértó, established by 1870 before being demolished at an unrecorded time; descendants of Újfehértó's Jews fenced the site in 1980 and erected two memorials, one in Hungarian and one in Hebrew. The town's small Jewish community grew through the 18th century, declined after 1840 when Jews gained permission to settle in major cities, then rebounded significantly with an influx of Galician refugees around WWI; by 1941, 1,359 Jews (of 15,154 residents) lived there. Following German occupation, the community was transferred to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz in May 1944. A few survivors returned but all left by 1948, ending Jewish presence in the city entirely.
